questions.question: A Kafka cluster with replication.factor=3 and min.insync.replicas=2 experiences a broker failure. If a producer uses acks=all, what happens when two out of three brokers for a partition are unavailable?
options: The producer will receive a success response as long as one broker acknowledges
The producer will receive a NotEnoughReplicasException
The producer will wait indefinitely until all brokers are available
The producer request is automatically redirected to another partition
questions.answer: The producer will receive a NotEnoughReplicasException
questions.explanation: With acks=all and min.insync.replicas=2, the producer requires acknowledgment from at least 2 replicas. When only 1 replica is available, it cannot satisfy this requirement, resulting in NotEnoughReplicasException.

questions.question: A producer application is sending high volumes of data to Kafka with batch.size=16384 and linger.ms=0. To improve throughput, the team increases batch.size to 32768 but sees minimal improvement. What configuration change would most effectively increase throughput?
options: Increase max.in.flight.requests.per.connection
Set linger.ms=10
Set acks=1 instead of acks=all
Enable compression.type=snappy
questions.answer: Set linger.ms=10
questions.explanation: With linger.ms=0, batches are sent immediately regardless of batch.size. Setting linger.ms>0 allows time for batches to fill before sending, significantly improving throughput when message production rate doesn't immediately fill batches.

questions.question: An application processes messages using a consumer with enable.auto.commit=true and auto.commit.interval.ms=5000. If the application crashes after processing records but before the auto-commit interval triggers, what scenario occurs when the application restarts?
options: All processed records will be processed again due to uncommitted offsets
No records will be processed again because offsets are stored in memory
Only records received in the last 5 seconds will be processed again
The application will pick up from the last message it was processing
questions.answer: All processed records will be processed again due to uncommitted offsets
questions.explanation: With auto-commits, offsets are only committed every auto.commit.interval.ms period. If the application crashes before the interval triggers, no offsets are committed, causing all processed messages to be consumed again on restart.

questions.question: A Kafka Streams application with 4 instances is processing data from a topic with 8 partitions. If a 5th instance is added, what happens?
options: The 5th instance will remain idle as there are only 8 partitions for 4 instances
The 5th instance will cause rebalancing, with some partitions being reassigned to it
The 5th instance will only get assigned if an existing instance fails
The 5th instance will automatically increase the partitions to 10
questions.answer: The 5th instance will cause rebalancing, with some partitions being reassigned to it
questions.explanation: When a new instance joins, Kafka Streams triggers a rebalance, redistributing the partitions across all instances including the new one. Each instance can process multiple partitions, so the 5th instance will get assigned partitions.

questions.question: In an Avro schema, adding a new field without a default value is what type of schema evolution?
options: Backward compatible
Forward compatible
Fully compatible
Breaking compatibility
questions.answer: Forward compatible
questions.explanation: Adding a field without a default value is forward compatible: new consumers (with the new schema) can read data produced with the old schema because they know to use defaults, but old consumers can't read new data as they don't know how to handle the new field.

questions.question: A JDBC Source Connector is configured to import data from 4 database tables into Kafka. The connector is created with max.tasks=2 deployed on a cluster with 5 workers. How many tasks will be launched?
options: 4 tasks (one per table)
2 tasks (as specified by max.tasks)
5 tasks (one per worker)
1 task (JDBC connector defaults to single-task mode)
questions.answer: 2 tasks (as specified by max.tasks)
questions.explanation: The JDBC Source Connector can create multiple tasks, but the max.tasks setting limits the maximum number of tasks that can be created, regardless of how many tables are being imported or how many workers are available.

questions.question: A Kafka cluster has SSL enabled for data encryption. Which Kafka performance optimization is lost when using SSL?
options: Batch compression
Zero-copy optimization
Client-side partitioning
Producer batching
questions.answer: Zero-copy optimization
questions.explanation: Zero-copy optimization allows Kafka to transfer data directly from the file system to the network without copying it into user space. SSL requires data to be loaded into the JVM for encryption/decryption, eliminating the zero-copy advantage.

questions.question: A compacted topic has a record with key K and value V1. Later, a new message arrives with key K and value V2. Finally, a tombstone message with key K and null value arrives. After compaction runs, what will exist in the log for key K?
options: K:V1 (first message keeps precedence)
K:V2 (last non-null value remains)
Nothing (tombstone removes all messages with that key)
K:null (tombstone value is preserved)
questions.answer: Nothing (tombstone removes all messages with that key)
questions.explanation: Log compaction preserves the most recent value for each key. When a tombstone (null value) is the most recent message for a key, after compaction runs, all messages with that key (including the tombstone itself) will be removed.

questions.question: When is log compaction triggered in Kafka?
options: Every time a message is sent to Kafka
Every time a message is flushed to disk
Every time a segment is closed if the dirty ratio threshold is met
Every time a new partition is created
questions.answer: Every time a segment is closed if the dirty ratio threshold is met
questions.explanation: Log compaction is evaluated when a segment is closed. It will be triggered if enough data is 'dirty' (eligible for compaction) according to the configured dirty ratio threshold.

questions.question: In a Kafka cluster configured with multiple log retention settings (log.retention.hours=168, log.retention.minutes=10080, log.retention.ms=604800000), which one takes precedence?
options: log.retention.hours takes precedence
log.retention.ms takes precedence
log.retention.minutes takes precedence
The smallest resulting retention period takes precedence
questions.answer: The smallest resulting retention period takes precedence
questions.explanation: When multiple retention settings are specified, Kafka uses the configuration that results in the smallest retention period. In this case, all values equal 7 days, so they're equivalent.

questions.question: A developer notices duplicated messages in a Kafka topic. The producer configuration shows retries=3 and max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=5. What configuration change would prevent duplicates without reducing throughput?
options: Set retries=0
Enable the idempotent producer with enable.idempotence=true
Set max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=1
Decrease request.timeout.ms
questions.answer: Enable the idempotent producer with enable.idempotence=true
questions.explanation: The idempotent producer guarantees exactly-once delivery semantics between producer and broker, preventing duplicates even with retries. Unlike setting max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=1, it doesn't reduce throughput.

questions.question: A consumer group with 5 consumers is processing a topic with 10 partitions. If 3 more consumers join the group, what will happen?
options: The new consumers will remain idle until someone leaves
Each of the 8 consumers will process exactly one partition, with 2 partitions unassigned
All 8 consumers will be active with some processing more partitions than others
The rebalance will fail because there are more consumers than needed
questions.answer: All 8 consumers will be active with some processing more partitions than others
questions.explanation: Kafka assigns partitions to consumers in a consumer group. With 10 partitions and 8 consumers, each consumer will get at least one partition, but some will handle two partitions to cover all 10.

questions.question: A Kafka Streams application needs to join a KStream with reference data that changes infrequently. Which approach is most efficient if the reference data isn't distributed across the same number of partitions?
options: Repartition the KStream to match the reference data's partitioning
Use a KTable join with co-partitioning
Use a GlobalKTable for the reference data
Use a foreign-key join
questions.answer: Use a GlobalKTable for the reference data
questions.explanation: GlobalKTable replicates the entire data to each instance and doesn't require co-partitioning for joins. It's ideal for reference data that changes infrequently and needs to be joined with a KStream, regardless of partitioning.

questions.question: A team using Schema Registry with multiple applications notices that schema evolution is being rejected despite configuring BACKWARD compatibility. What is the most likely cause?
options: The schema is being registered with a different subject name
The schema requires FORWARD compatibility instead
The schema contains complex types not supported by Avro
One application is using JsonSerializer instead of AvroSerializer
questions.answer: The schema contains complex types not supported by Avro
questions.explanation: BACKWARD compatibility ensures new consumers can read old data. The most likely issue is that the new schema contains complex types or structure changes that break the compatibility rules, not a configuration issue.

questions.question: A JDBC Sink Connector is being used to write data from a Kafka topic with 15 partitions to a database. If max.tasks=5, what effect will increasing to max.tasks=20 have?
options: 20 tasks will be created, each handling a portion of the topic's data
Only 15 tasks will be created, limited by the number of partitions
5 tasks will still be used, as the workers need to be increased first
The connector will fail as max.tasks exceeds the partition count
questions.answer: Only 15 tasks will be created, limited by the number of partitions
questions.explanation: For a Sink Connector, the maximum number of tasks that can be created is limited by the number of partitions in the topic. With 15 partitions, at most 15 tasks can be created, regardless of the max.tasks setting.

questions.question: A Kafka cluster has ACLs enabled. A developer moves a producer application to a new server and it fails with authorization errors. What's the likely cause?
options: The developer didn't update the JAAS configuration file
The ACL is bound to the previous server's hostname or IP address
The producer is attempting to write to a different topic
The SSL certificates haven't been copied to the new server
questions.answer: The ACL is bound to the previous server's hostname or IP address
questions.explanation: Kafka ACLs can include a 'Host' filter that restricts permissions to specific IPs or hostnames. When moving to a new server with a different IP, the existing ACL won't allow access from the new location.

questions.question: A topic is configured with cleanup.policy=compact,delete, retention.ms=86400000, and min.cleanable.dirty.ratio=0.5. How will the log cleanup behave?
options: Messages older than 1 day will be deleted first, then remaining messages will be compacted
Messages will be compacted, and any remaining messages older than 1 day will be deleted
Either compaction or deletion will occur independently, whichever threshold is reached first
The policies conflict and the broker will use the default (deletion)
questions.answer: Messages older than 1 day will be deleted first, then remaining messages will be compacted
questions.explanation: With both compact and delete policies, Kafka first applies the deletion policy to remove old segments, then compaction runs on the remaining segments. The compaction will only occur if the min.cleanable.dirty.ratio threshold is met.

questions.question: In a Kafka cluster with 5 brokers, how is the Controller selected?
options: The broker with the lowest broker.id becomes the Controller
The first broker to create a particular znode in ZooKeeper becomes the Controller
The broker with the highest uptime is selected as the Controller
Administrators manually assign a broker to be the Controller
questions.answer: The first broker to create a particular znode in ZooKeeper becomes the Controller
questions.explanation: The Controller in Kafka is elected based on which broker first successfully creates an ephemeral node in ZooKeeper. It's not predetermined based on broker.id or other attributes.

questions.question: A consumer processes records that take 8 minutes per batch. After upgrading Kafka, the consumer keeps disconnecting and triggering rebalances. What's the most likely cause?
options: The consumer.id format changed in the new version
The max.poll.interval.ms default was decreased in the new version
The session.timeout.ms default was increased in the new version
The heartbeat.interval.ms is causing too much network traffic
questions.answer: The max.poll.interval.ms default was decreased in the new version
questions.explanation: max.poll.interval.ms controls the maximum time between poll() calls before a consumer is considered failed. If this default decreased in the new version, and processing takes 8 minutes, the consumer would be disconnected before finishing processing.

questions.question: A producer sends a message with a key to a topic with 10 partitions. Later, the topic is expanded to 20 partitions. What happens to messages with the same key?
options: New messages will go to the same partition as before
New messages may go to a different partition than before
The key hash calculation ensures partition consistency regardless of partition count
The producer needs to be restarted to recognize the new partition count
questions.answer: New messages may go to a different partition than before
questions.explanation: When partition count changes, the key hashing algorithm (typically key.hashCode() % numPartitions) results in different partition assignments. This breaks the guarantee that 'same key goes to same partition'.

questions.question: A Kafka Streams application needs to calculate a moving average over a 5-minute window, updated every minute. Which window type should be used?
options: Tumbling window
Hopping window
Session window
Sliding window
questions.answer: Hopping window
questions.explanation: Hopping windows have fixed sizes and advance by a specified interval, creating overlapping windows. A 5-minute window advancing every minute creates exactly the moving average behavior required.

questions.question: Where does Schema Registry store schemas?
options: In ZooKeeper
In the Schema Registry's embedded SQL database
In the _schemas topic in Kafka
In the message bytes themselves
questions.answer: In the _schemas topic in Kafka
questions.explanation: Schema Registry stores all schemas in the _schemas Kafka topic, not in ZooKeeper or an embedded database. This provides durability and simplifies Schema Registry deployment.

questions.question: What happens if a Single Message Transform in a Kafka Connect pipeline throws an exception while processing a record?
options: The connector automatically skips that record and continues processing
The connector fails and needs to be restarted manually
The record is sent to a dead letter queue if configured, otherwise the connector fails
The record is retried indefinitely until it succeeds
questions.answer: The record is sent to a dead letter queue if configured, otherwise the connector fails
questions.explanation: By default, any transformation error causes connector failure. With errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name configured, failed records go to that topic and the connector continues processing.

questions.question: In a Kafka cluster with SASL/SCRAM authentication, what must be configured on the broker side?
options: A list of allowed users with usernames and passwords in server.properties
A reference to an external LDAP server in server.properties
At least one SCRAM credential created using kafka-configs.sh tool
Nothing; SASL/SCRAM doesn't require broker-side configuration
questions.answer: At least one SCRAM credential created using kafka-configs.sh tool
questions.explanation: For SASL/SCRAM, brokers need credentials created with the kafka-configs.sh tool using the --add-config option specifying users and passwords. These credentials are stored in ZooKeeper, not in server.properties.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the high watermark in Kafka?
options: It prevents brokers from running out of disk space
It indicates the maximum disk space allowed for a partition
It defines the latest offset that all in-sync replicas have received
It sets the maximum number of messages that can be sent per second
questions.answer: It defines the latest offset that all in-sync replicas have received
questions.explanation: The high watermark is the offset of the last message that has been successfully replicated to all in-sync replicas. Consumers can only read up to this offset, ensuring they only see messages that won't be lost if the leader fails.

questions.question: A 9-node ZooKeeper ensemble is used for a Kafka cluster. How many ZooKeeper servers can fail before the ensemble can't function?
options: 2 servers
3 servers
4 servers
5 servers
questions.answer: 4 servers
questions.explanation: A ZooKeeper ensemble requires a majority (quorum) to function. For a 9-node ensemble, the quorum is 5 nodes (majority). Therefore, it can tolerate up to 4 node failures while maintaining a quorum of 5.

questions.question: A consumer using enable.auto.commit=false crashes after processing messages but before committing offsets. What happens when it restarts?
options: It will start from where it crashed, using ZooKeeper's saved state
It will start from the latest offset in the partition
It will start from the earliest offset in the partition
It will start from the last committed offset, reprocessing all messages since then
questions.answer: It will start from the last committed offset, reprocessing all messages since then
questions.explanation: Without auto-commit, a consumer must explicitly commit offsets. If it crashes before committing, it will restart from the last successfully committed offset, reprocessing all messages processed since that commit.

questions.question: What determines the maximum parallelism of a Kafka Streams application?
options: The num.stream.threads configuration setting
The number of partitions in the input topics
The number of application instances deployed
The number of machines in the Kafka cluster
questions.answer: The number of partitions in the input topics
questions.explanation: Kafka Streams parallelism is limited by the number of input topic partitions. Each partition can only be processed by one task at a time, so adding more instances beyond the partition count won't increase parallelism.

questions.question: A topic has 6 partitions with replication.factor=3. After adding 3 new brokers to the cluster (for a total of 6), what happens to the partition distribution?
options: Partitions are automatically rebalanced across all 6 brokers
New partitions will use the new brokers, but existing partitions stay on their original brokers
No change occurs until partition reassignment is manually triggered
Only leader replicas move to the new brokers
questions.answer: No change occurs until partition reassignment is manually triggered
questions.explanation: Kafka doesn't automatically redistribute existing partitions when brokers are added. A manual partition reassignment is required to rebalance partitions across the expanded broker set.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to perform real-time analytics on payment transactions coming into a Kafka topic. The analytics team has strong SQL skills but minimal programming experience. What's the best approach?
options: Implement a Kafka Streams application with a SQL-like DSL
Use ksqlDB to create streams and materialized views of the transaction data
Deploy Kafka Connect with a JDBC sink connector to write to an analytics database
Write a custom consumer that processes the data and queries an SQL database
questions.answer: Use ksqlDB to create streams and materialized views of the transaction data
questions.explanation: ksqlDB provides SQL-like syntax for stream processing, making it ideal for SQL-skilled teams with minimal programming experience. It allows creating streams and tables directly from Kafka topics with familiar SQL syntax.

questions.question: A team is using Kafka Connect with JSON data and encounters this error: 'JsonDeserializer with schemas.enable requires schema and payload fields'. What's the solution?
options: Set schemas.enable=false in the connector configuration
Add schema and payload fields to every JSON message
Switch to using AvroConverter instead of JsonConverter
Configure a Single Message Transform to add schema fields
questions.answer: Set schemas.enable=false in the connector configuration
questions.explanation: This error occurs when using JsonConverter with schemas.enable=true on plain JSON without schema and payload wrapper fields. Setting key.converter.schemas.enable=false and value.converter.schemas.enable=false fixes it.

questions.question: A producer application occasionally receives TimeoutExceptions when sending large messages. Which configuration would most effectively resolve this issue?
options: Increase linger.ms to batch more messages
Increase request.timeout.ms to allow more time for broker responses
Enable compression to reduce message size
Increase max.block.ms to allow more time for buffer space to free up
questions.answer: Increase request.timeout.ms to allow more time for broker responses
questions.explanation: TimeoutExceptions occur when the broker doesn't respond within request.timeout.ms. Large messages take longer to process, so increasing this timeout gives the broker more time to handle large messages before timing out.

questions.question: A consumer application performs complex calculations on each message, averaging 30 seconds per batch. When deployed in production, it triggers rebalances every few minutes. How can this be fixed?
options: Decrease session.timeout.ms to accommodate the processing time
Increase max.poll.interval.ms to exceed the processing time
Use manual partition assignment instead of subscribe()
Decrease max.poll.records to process fewer records per batch
questions.answer: Increase max.poll.interval.ms to exceed the processing time
questions.explanation: max.poll.interval.ms limits how long a consumer can go between poll() calls. With 30-second processing, the default (5 minutes) should be enough, but production might have larger batches. Increasing this value prevents premature rebalances.

questions.question: A Kafka Streams application using RocksDB for state storage restarts frequently due to container orchestration. What can be done to significantly reduce recovery time?
options: Increase the number of stream threads
Mount a persistent volume for RocksDB
Decrease state.cleanup.delay.ms
Enable standby replicas for the state stores
questions.answer: Mount a persistent volume for RocksDB
questions.explanation: With a persistent volume, RocksDB state is preserved across restarts, avoiding full recovery from Kafka changelog topics. This dramatically reduces restart time since only missing updates need to be recovered.

questions.question: What protocol does the Schema Registry use for client communication?
options: The Kafka binary protocol
HTTP/HTTPS REST
SASL/PLAIN over TLS
A custom binary protocol
questions.answer: HTTP/HTTPS REST
questions.explanation: Schema Registry exposes a REST API over HTTP/HTTPS for clients to register and retrieve schemas, not the Kafka binary protocol or other communication methods.

questions.question: Which metric is most important to monitor for detecting a consumer falling behind producers?
options: consumer-fetch-manager-metrics:records-lag-max
consumer-fetch-manager-metrics:records-consumed-rate
consumer-coordinator-metrics:commit-latency-avg
consumer-node-metrics:incoming-byte-rate
questions.answer: consumer-fetch-manager-metrics:records-lag-max
questions.explanation: records-lag-max shows the maximum lag in terms of number of records for any partition in the consumer group. It's the most direct indicator of a consumer falling behind producers.

questions.question: What does Kafka's zero-copy optimization refer to?
options: Not copying data between producer threads
Not making backup copies of messages on disk
Transferring data directly from file system cache to network socket
Avoiding copies by using reference counting for messages
questions.answer: Transferring data directly from file system cache to network socket
questions.explanation: Zero-copy optimization in Kafka transfers data directly from disk (or page cache) to the network socket without copying it into the application's memory, significantly improving throughput.

questions.question: Where are Kafka Connect offsets stored in distributed mode?
options: In ZooKeeper under /connect/offsets
In a dedicated Kafka topic specified by offset.storage.topic
In a file on each worker's local filesystem
In the __consumer_offsets topic
questions.answer: In a dedicated Kafka topic specified by offset.storage.topic
questions.explanation: In distributed mode, Kafka Connect stores connector offsets in a dedicated Kafka topic specified by the offset.storage.topic configuration, not in ZooKeeper or local files.

questions.question: A topic is used for storing user session data with cleanup.policy=compact. If User1 has multiple session records with the same key but different values, what will remain after compaction?
options: All session records for User1 will be preserved
Only the first session record for User1 will be preserved
Only the most recent session record for User1 will be preserved
All session records will be deleted during compaction
questions.answer: Only the most recent session record for User1 will be preserved
questions.explanation: Log compaction retains only the most recent message for each key. For User1's session data with the same key, only the latest record will be preserved after compaction runs.

questions.question: A financial application needs to ensure that only authorized clients can produce to sensitive topics. Which authentication mechanism provides the strongest security?
options: SASL/PLAIN
SASL/SCRAM
SSL/TLS with client certificates
IP-based filtering with allow_principal rules
questions.answer: SSL/TLS with client certificates
questions.explanation: SSL/TLS with client certificates provides the strongest security by verifying both server and client identities using PKI. Each client needs its own certificate, allowing precise control over client authentication.

questions.question: What happens if a consumer sets auto.offset.reset=none and tries to read from a partition with no committed offset?
options: It starts reading from the earliest available offset
It starts reading from the latest offset
It throws an exception and stops consuming
It creates a new consumer group
questions.answer: It throws an exception and stops consuming
questions.explanation: With auto.offset.reset=none,
